pageCache.pageTitle: St. James' CE First School and Nursery - Home
pageCache.text:
We follow Jesus’ example by valuing and cherishing all God’s children in an ever-changing world. We are loved so we can love.
St James’
St James' First School and Nursery is a wonderful village school, set in idyllic scenery, just outside the heart of Wimborne. We believe that success is all down to high expectations and aspirations for every child and we aim for excellence in everything we do.
School should be a joyful experience for all children; they only have one shot at primary education and the greatest responsibility we have is to get it right for them at the very beginning.
Are you exploring schools for September?
Admissions 2027
Latest News
Follow Us
Dear Parents and Carers, As the Summer sun continues unabated and the school field slowly turns a golden hue, our term finally has finally drawn to a close and I want to take this moment to share how incredibly proud I am of all our children, for all they have achieved this year and the community they have helped to build. Over the last few weeks, with the temperatures in the lunch hall reaching peak uncomfortable, we have taken to having our lunch as a picnic in the Peace Garden under the shade of the tree. It has been a joy to watch the children enjoy their lunch together and without the structure of the formal dining tables, build community beyond their immediate friendship group. As I have reflected on the successes of this year over the last few weeks, I have found myself drawn constantly back to this idea of belonging and the rich power it has to bring us all together. The behaviour and attitudes of others can have a huge influence on our own. When many people within a group (like a class or school) adopt a similar behaviour this 'social norm' effect becomes so powerful that it can often override more formal policies and rules. However, the strength of their influence rests heavily on how much we feel accepted and belong. In short, behaviour and learning are a product of 'belonging'. (Credit Peps McCrae) And, as the whole school stood hand in hand on stage at the Layard Theatre for our end of year show, (and I held back the tears) it was clear that we knew we all belonged, from the youngest to the oldest, from volunteer to staff member. That our 'norm' was something special and unique, something beautiful, because of our togetherness. When Paul wrote to the early church in Galatia, he emphasised the difference of the believers but how in Christ they could all find their belonging. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is no male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus. Galatians 3:28 Paul's message was one of unity and belonging. He knew that in this togetherness and belonging we find the strength we need to try our best, to demonstrate optimism and hope amid the darkness and to always be compassionate and loving to ourselves and our community. So, as I reflect on some key moments in our year, thank you for building our belonging, thank you for encouraging one another and thank you for setting an example for our children to follow. For our Year 4's, whose time is coming to a close, there have been moments throughout the year where they have demonstrated their belonging in abundance. In October, they joined with our 27 other Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust schools to perform a pop concert at Salisbury Cathedral. At Christmas, they became a class choir and travelled the community to spread some Christmas cheer to some of the most vulnerable in our community. And then in May, they travelled to Osmington Bay for our annual PGL Osmington Bay residential. Myself, along with the whole staff team, will miss our Year 4's but know they have been equipped with all the knowledge, skills and personal qualities to be a success on their next adventure. Along with our Year 4's, we also say goodbye to Miss Gudger. Starting as a midday supervisor over ten years ago, she has become a foundational member of our teaching assistant and pastoral team. As well as her essential role supporting classroom learning, she has led our pastoral team and delivered ELSA for over six years. As she begins her retirement, I want to thank her for all her years of service, her friendship and her unwavering commitment to encouraging those in need. Our year has also found its belonging in our community events. These have taken place in a variety of different forms from Parent Share Events, Remembrance Service, World Book Day, Easter Celebrations or Nativities – there is always so much joy to be found in our collective celebrations. The newest of these events was our first ever Art Exhibition which was a wonderful celebration of the creative arts. Over four days, each class worked with local artist Maria Vinney to celebrate Spring and its many colours. As the work was displayed, it was a joy to watch the children and parents not only celebrate their own work but also stop, pause and enjoy the work of their friends. We look forward to making our Art Exhibition a feature of our regular St James calendar. The celebration of the arts didn't stop there, Owls class learnt to play Samba with Dorset Music Service, Foxes learnt the glockenspiel and the whole school (including Nursery for the first time) performed traditional English dances as part of our May Pole celebrations. Our year of arts culminated in our End of Year show at The Layard Theatre which was a resounding success and in the words of the Wimborne Mayor, 'School theatre at its very best!' Of course, one of our core objectives as a school is to ensure all children make progress in their academic learning and I am delighted to once again share some outstanding results. In Reception, the percentage of children reaching the Good Level of Development (GLD) rose to 88% compared to a predicted national average of 69%. In the Year 1 phonics screening check, 100% of our children passed which is once again a tremendous achievement and highlights the strength of teaching in reading. And in our Year 4 Multiplication check, 100% of children scored above the unofficial pass mark of 20/25. In fact, with an average score of 24.0 and 60% of children scoring full marks (46% did this nationally) we are among the top achieving schools. Another area of resounding success is the continued growth of our Nursery provision. In September Miss Jay was appointed Nursery Lead and was later joined by Mrs Lawrence in January. Under their careful leadership, confidence has grown in our provision and bookings continue to flourish for next year with a 25% growth year on year. To support this growth, we have grown the Nursery team and Mrs Hardyman and Mrs Ryan will be joining the team next year. As the Nursery continues to grow over the year, we are hoping to increase Forest School as part of the provision and will replicate the impact it has on the well-being and cohesiveness of our reception class with our youngest learners, so watch this space Nursery families. I also find great hope and joy in our continued Trust collaboration. For our Year 3 and 4 children, the Priory cup was a resounding success with Football, Netball, Rounders and Athletics tournaments hosted across our four schools. Thank you to all those who not only competed and represented the school but did so with a sense of togetherness. For our staff team, the Trust provides a wealth of professional development opportunities and a structure through which we continually look for school improvements. So, as we begin take to stock and look ahead into next year, it is clear that the landscape of education remains incredibly challenging with further unfunded pay rises and rising costs forcing all schools into what the Government call efficiency savings. We also received the shock news last month that the Government has cancelled the Sports Premium funding which has supported many of our sporting activities. But I am relentlessly optimistic and will always look to utilise the opportunities available beyond the traditional income avenues to make our school a success. Earlier this week we received £1200 in funding from West Mercia Energy – I have my fingers crossed for the many other bids I have made. Of course, our St James' PFA also continue to heavily invest in the life of the school by creating and supporting all our events and raising vital funds to ensure we can provide the best possible outcomes for our children. Earlier this week, one of my team made a comment that the Peace Garden has become a hub of many of our events. It has played host to our picnic lunches, we used it as a venue for Miss Gudger's retirement gathering and on Wednesday morning we said a well-deserved 'Thank You' to our whole community. It was however in April that it became a focus of our celebration for beloved Tilly who lost her battle with cancer. Tilly was a bright and joy filled member of our community who demonstrated such resilience in the face of adversity. As part of our remembering, every child planted a butterfly in our garden. The butterfly holds a fragile beauty that hides the incredible transformation that took place. All who knew and loved Tilly understood how her infectious joy was transformational. As the children of St James' left school on Wednesday, they have each brought home a butterfly as a way of remembering Tilly. They have now flown the garden and will live on in our homes and hearts forever. It is in both the highs and the lows that belonging finds space to flourish. Whether it is the collective tears shared together, or hands held on stage to the final applause, it is in our belonging where our love, hope and truth can resound. So, as we prepare for the summer holidays, I want to thank every member of our community for their love and hope this year. It is a joy and a privilege to lead such a fantastic team, shepherd such wonderful children and encourage such a supportive community. Please find time to enjoy the sun, time with friends and family and I very much look forward to welcoming you back to all the joys that our new year will bring. Yours faithfully, Mr Lawford
Yesterday we said a very special goodbye to our wonderful Nursery leavers. We gathered in the Peace Garden for a beautiful ceremony, where the children shared artwork, performed a song and recited a poem to their families. We then finished off with delicious cakes kindly donated by St James' PFA. We're so proud of each and every one of our Nursery leavers and all they have achieved during their time with us, and we've no doubt they'll continue to shine as they begin their next adventure in Foxes!
All the staff at St James' First School and Nursery - Wimborne want to say huge congratulations to the children for an incredible end of year performance! The Jungle Book was a resounding success, alive with colour, music and dance! You were all amazing and have so much to be proud of! You have learnt so many lines, rehearsed so many dances and put on a spectacle that will be remembered for years to come. Our end of year show is part of our St James' DNA and we are so priveleged to be able to share it with you. Our show screams, 'I belong' and when we look back we can all say, 'We did it!' It doesn't matter if you are the youngest reception child, a year 4 leaver, teaching assistant, teacher or volunteer we all get to say, 'We did it,' and that gives us all a rich sense of belonging. We want to extend our thanks to everyone who made the performance such a resounding success. To the parents and volunteers who helped source and prepare costumes and all those whove supported your children learning lines and dance moves. To all the staff who have come together and offered countless additional hours, preparing materials, rehearsing scenes and painting scenary. To the St James' PFA for running our refreshments and pushing the DVD sales. Finally, to Vanessa who works with us as a volunteer and directed our show. She has invester hundreds of hours, helping the children rehearse, choreographed dances and running weekly drama club over the last term. As always, we were blessed to perform at The Layard Theatre at Canford School which is just an incredible venue and provides such a rich experience for all our children.
What a fantastic day Hedgehogs had in our Forest School. We started our day learning about how to be safe around a fire and making a fire together. We then whittled sticks, made our own bread dough before wrapping it around the sticks and cooking it in the fire. After out picnic lunch we made dens and create beautiful natural art! A massive thank you to Mrs Shergold, Mrs Hobbs and all our parent helpers who made the day so special.
It was a privelege to welcome The Creature Teachers to St James' First School and Nursery for a whole day of creature exploration. We met a blue tongue skink, a royal python, two ferrets, millipedes and a barn owl and were able to get hands on with the creatures. A huge thank you to St James' PFA for funding this special day which was a resounding success.
We are looking to appoint a part-time Nursery Practitioner to join our flourishing team from September. For more information, please contact the school office. https://mynewterm.com/jobs/148300/EDV-2026-SJCEFS-24087
Before the heatwave took hold, Year 4 refined their cycling skills as they all completed their Level 1 Bikeability. Children focused on controlling their bike, pedalling without wobble and being aware of their surroundings whilst turning. They all did brilliantly and passed with flying colours.
Look at these happy little feet! Our topic in Nursery is 'Under The Sea', so today we took a little trip to the beach for a lovely sensory activity. The children used some brilliant language to describe how the sand and water felt and had lots of fun mixing them both together to change the consistency and texture.
Last term in Nursery we introduced some tiny caterpillars to support our topic of Life Cycles, and our focus story of The Hungry Cat

pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
We are able to offer full wraparound care for all children at St James'. The extended school offer utilises the Cottage Building and provides the children with a friendly, inclusive environment with a wide range of planned activities.
Breakfast Club
Breakfast club is available to all children from 3 years of age. They will be able to start their day with a healthy breakfast of cereal, toast or fruit. The breakfast club runs from 7:45 am – 8:30 am and the children have a range of fun activities that they can take part in. A member of staff will take them to their classroom for registration at 8.30 am.
Breakfast Club Rate: £4.50
After-School Club
Our after-school club service is open to children from 3-9 years from 3 – 6 pm. If your child attends St James First school, they are collected directly from the first school and escorted to the cottage by a member of staff, all children are offered a healthy snack and drink.
After-School Club Rate: £5 per hour

pageCache.pageTitle: St. James' CE First School and Nursery - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Our Curriculum is firmly rooted in our Christian Vision: 'Believe and Achieve', underpinned by this verse from the Bible: ‘I will show you my faith by my deeds.’ James 2: 18
Our associated values of Love, Hope and Truth are woven through our Curriculum and help to develop the attitudes and dispositions that we want to instill in our children.
Through a carefully sequenced and progressive curriculum we seek to enable and inspire children to develop the confidence, knowledge, skills and creativity they need to flourish in a world of constant change.
The National Curriculum
The school follows the 2014 National Curriculum but we design and sequence each unit of learning very carefully to ensure progression within every subject and to meet the needs of our children. If you would like to find out more the National Curriculum and the content of our curriculum by subject and year group, click here.
Relevant, real life and exciting opportunities are planned as often as possible to enthuse children and give purpose to their learning. Opportunities include talking to professional actors to support our theme which culminates in a live performance in a professional theatre; a residential for our Year 4 children and visits to places such as Streetwise. We also give children the chance to contribute to the local community by organising fundraising opportunities and we welcome visitors to the school such as local paramedics and the Life Education Centre.
At St James, all teachers are responsible for providing an inclusive curriculum so that children with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEND) have equal access to the curriculum. We have high expectations for all pupils and are committed to ensuring our curriculum complies with the Equality Act 2010 and the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014.
We aim to challenge that mindset that seeks to predetermine the capacity of each learner, replacing it instead with a curiosity about what the learner can achieve. As teachers we should approach teaching with a sense of openness, looking to be surprised by our learners and what they can achieve.
...our curriculum should whisper to our children, “You belong. You did not come from nowhere. All this came before you, and one day you too might add to it.”(Ben Newmark)
Through the design of our curriculum and its implementation, we aim to create learning spaces where all children belong. At St James how we build a fully inclusive space for all and particularly those learners experiencing disadvantage, is crucial.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. James' CE First School and Nursery - Early Years
pageCache.text:
Early Years
At James' First School, we provide a high-quality EYFS education giving children a secure and confident start to their school life. We are committed to nurturing a lifelong love of learning alongside the aims of the EYFS statutory framework. We strive for high standards, consider the development of the whole child and seek to foster resilience and independence. We carefully plan the essential knowledge that children need to prepare them for their future success, to give children the best possible start to their early education.
We provide inviting classroom environments indoors and outdoors to stimulate learners and engage them in developing the three ‘Characteristics of Effective Learning’ as set out within the EYFS.
